name: Steve Cohen
bio: Memphis-area Democratic congressman serving since 2007. Announced May 15, 2026 he would not seek reelection after redistricting dismantled TN-9, but left the door open if legal challenges succeed. cohenforcongress.com remains active and he cosponsored the Universal School Meals Program Act of 2026 (H.R. 8798) in May 2026.
status_line: Conditional retirement announced May 15, 2026 · Active if redistricting lawsuit succeeds

early_childhood_ed.summary: Cohen has a long record of securing federal funding for Head Start, Early Head Start, and pre-K programs in the Memphis area. In June 2026, he took action to protect vulnerable children enrolled in the state's Children's Special Services program, urging Governor Lee to revoke a directive that would require approximately 400 sick or disabled children to report their immigration status to state enforcement authorities.
early_childhood_ed.details: Cohen sent a letter to Governor Bill Lee on June 17, 2026, calling the directive 'morally repulsive' and 'inhumane,' and questioning its legal basis given that the Tennessee law requiring immigration status verification applies to persons '18 years of age or older.' The Children's Special Services program serves low-income children from birth to age 21 with disabilities or serious illness, including children dependent on ventilators, feeding tubes, and wheelchairs. More than 4,600 Tennessee children received services through the program in 2024. Cohen also announced $2.8 million in NIH grants to St. Jude Children's Research Hospital during the week of June 26, 2026. Cohen is retiring from Congress in 2026 after a GOP-led redistricting split his district in three; his candidacy is no longer active. His advocacy on behalf of children's health programs represents his final legislative actions in office.

child_hunger.summary: Cohen cosponsored H.R. 8798 (Universal School Meals Program Act of 2026, May 13, 2026), which would provide free meals to every student nationwide and reverse SNAP cuts enacted by the One Big Beautiful Bill. In June 2026, approximately 100,000 Tennesseans lost SNAP benefits following the One Big Beautiful Bill's implementation, and Cohen's letter on behalf of sick immigrant children also underscored his broader commitment to protecting public benefits for vulnerable populations.
child_hunger.details: Cohen's May 2026 cosponsor action on H.R. 8798 remains his most direct recent legislative statement on child hunger, proposing universal free breakfast, lunch, dinner, and a snack for every student, along with expanded Summer EBT (SUN Bucks). The broader Tennessee SNAP landscape in June 2026 saw approximately 100,000 residents lose benefits under One Big Beautiful Bill cuts, with enrollment falling from 696,000 in July 2025 to about 598,000 by May 2026. A federal judge on June 23, 2026 temporarily blocked Tennessee's planned July restrictions on SNAP-eligible food items (limiting junk food purchases). Cohen's June 17 letter defending Children's Special Services recipients also implicitly supports maintaining public benefits for children regardless of immigration status. Cohen is not running for reelection; his June 2026 activities represent his final months in office.

parental_support.summary: Cohen reintroduced the Latonya Reeves Freedom Act in June 2026 with 48 bipartisan cosponsors, a disability rights bill that would codify the right to home- and community-based long-term care services — directly supporting families of children with complex medical needs. His June 17, 2026 letter defending sick and disabled children in the Children's Special Services program reflects an ongoing commitment to protecting services that support these families.
parental_support.details: The Latonya Reeves Freedom Act, reintroduced by Cohen in June 2026 with bipartisan support, would bar government entities and insurers from denying home- and community-based services to eligible individuals, honoring the Supreme Court's Olmstead ruling on disability rights. The bill is named after a Memphis woman who had to leave Tennessee to access independent living services. Cohen's earlier legislative record includes cosponsoring the FAMILY Act for national paid family leave and voting in February 2024 to expand the Child Tax Credit. No new paid family leave or Child Tax Credit legislation was identified in the June 14–29, 2026 window. Cohen is retiring from Congress in 2026 after redistricting eliminated the seat he represented for 19 years.
